Weights were the standard maximums (2.95 kg cock, 2.5 kg hen); Poultrykeeper gives cock 2.5 to 2.95 kg and hen 2.0 to 2.5 kg, so set rooster 2.7 kg and hen 2.3 kg. summary.value: The Marsh Daisy is a rare English chicken from Southport in Lancashire. Breeding began in the 1880s with an Old English Game cock and Malay hens, and Hamburgh, Leghorn and Sicilian Buttercup blood was added later; the type was settled by 1913. The name may come from its marshy home or from its large rose comb, said to look like the sea thrift flower. It has white earlobes and willow green legs, and the usual colors are wheaten, brown, buff and black. It is a light bird: cocks weigh about 5.5 to 6.5 pounds and hens about 4.5 to 5.5. Hens lay around 160 to 210 tinted eggs a year. Birds grow slowly but are hardy once grown, forage well and do best on free range. They are mostly calm but active, can fly and may be flighty. There is no bantam form.
